note: Almost everything on this site was read from Italy's online registers, through a screen. These are the places that stops. Each ask below is something an archive, a museum or a library holds and does not put online, so it needs an order, a letter or a visit, not a search. They come from this archive's own questions and work list, where each is marked blocked or not attempted. None is recorded as sent, and none as answered.

doors.why: Forchia and Arpaia are in Benevento province, a different tribunale from the Caserta registers this archive has read. Two annual birth volumes are not digitised, and the military record of one man born in 1895 is held there.

asks.what: Forchia births, 1897: the act of Filomena Annecchino, born 10 April 1897
asks.ref: Not on Antenati: its Forchia births run 1895, 1896, 1898, 1899 with no 1897 in any fondo or either archive. FamilySearch: Benevento Civil Registration (State Archive) 1810-1942, collection 2475030
asks.why: Without it the descent from Carmine Annecchino and Maria Carfora is reconstructed, not documented. FamilySearch's index covers Forchia in 1897 (about thirty records a year) and yet returns no child of 1897 for Carmine and Maria, and no Filomena born between 1895 and 1899. Her Queensland death registration, 1988/6856, gives the birth year 1897 and her father as Carmine, so the birth is not in doubt. The act is missing or misfiled.
asks.ask: The Forchia births volume for 1897, ordered or read at the archive, and the act of 10 April 1897.

asks.what: Arpaia births, 1895: the act of Angelo Zampiello's birth
asks.ref: Not digitised: the shelf-marks run consecutively and skip 1895, confirmed from Antenati's own holdings list
asks.why: His birth date is corroborated by his memorial card, but the act itself is unread.
asks.ask: The Arpaia births volume for 1895, ordered or read at the archive, and his act.

asks.what: Angelo Zampiello's foglio matricolare, his military record
asks.why: The family's own papers hold the Croce al Merito di Guerra conferred on him for operations in East Africa from 3 October 1935. The family's account is that it was for saving many lives. A merit cross is given for service in a theatre, and gallantry would ordinarily carry a Medaglia al Valor Militare, so the account is not yet settled. The record would also give the First World War service of a man born in 1895, which is entirely untraced.

doors.where: The Museo Alfonsiano and the parish of Sant'Andrea, Arienzo
doors.why: The museum stands in the old bishop's palace beside Sant'Andrea, the church this family was baptised in for two centuries.

asks.what: Whether either holds, or knows of, parish material that was never filmed
asks.ref: Open questions: The Museo Alfonsiano, Arienzo; The Arienzo parish baptism register, liber IX
asks.why: The Arienzo baptism register cited in the 1814 marriage dossier (liber IX, folios 47v and 94v) is still listed as an open question. FamilySearch's full-text search has since returned Arienzo baptism images from the 1760s onward, so what the parish could add beyond the film is not yet known.

doors.where: A FamilySearch centre or an affiliate library
doors.why: Several Caserta record images return "This record can only be displayed on certain accounts". The index and the machine transcriptions are open; the scans are not. A centre or an affiliate library unlocks them.

asks.what: Read the restricted Caserta scans in person
asks.ref: Which images is not itemised on the work list
asks.why: Almost everything on this site rests on the open index and transcriptions. The scans would let a reader check them against the page.
asks.ask: A visit to a centre or an affiliate library.
